note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published by PlayStation (Exophase / PSNProfiles, 18 Nov 2026). Every guide below is written in our own words from the official description and the PSN progress target where one exists. The game launched on 19 Nov 2026: where a place or step is not pinned down yet, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing one.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work through the roadmap in this guide in order: story first, then the side characters, the activities, the collectibles, and the long grinds last. Community estimates put the full run at roughly 200 hours, so treat this as a long project rather than a weekend. Every trophy below is tracked on this page, so this is your finish line.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: it pops automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. Play with your partner beside you — Jason and Lucia together — then build a 4-star wanted level and break away until it clears. The practical way: get the heat in a fast car on the edge of town, then drive out of the search area, ditch the car, and stay out of sight until the stars fade. Do not let your partner get caught or killed mid-escape, or the attempt fails.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: you can retry a wanted-level escape as often as you like.

trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. With your partner beside you, rob three shops in a row — and do not let the wanted level drop between them. Plan a route first: three shops close together, a fast getaway car parked nearby, and no long drives between stops. Rob the first, keep the heat, hit the second and third quickly, then lose the cops only after the third robbery. If the wanted level clears between shops, the chain breaks and you start over.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: you can retry the three-shop chain as often as you like.

trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode. The setup matters more than the shooting: find a spot with five or more enemies grouped together, trigger Combat Focus, and drop all five before it runs out. A mission or a gang hideout with clustered enemies is the natural place to try it. If you only get three or four, reload and try a busier spot — the trophy needs all five in one activation.

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. The name says it: succeed on a second try. The exact trigger has not been confirmed in the game yet — it most likely pops when you fail something and then succeed at the same thing on your next attempt, whether a mission, a challenge or an activity. Play normally and it will probably pop on its own; if it does not, retry a failed challenge immediately and finish it second time round.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: it triggers on a retry, so it can happen at any point.

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? This is a strange-encounter trophy — the description is the reaction, not the instruction. The trigger has not been confirmed in the game yet, and several guides list it as one of the trophies with no confirmed method at launch. It most likely pops when you witness or trigger an odd event somewhere in Leonida: a UFO-style moment, a weird NPC, or something out of place. Explore the odd corners of the map and keep an eye out for anything unusual.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: strange encounters can be found after the story.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. Knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a drive-by with a bat or a similar melee weapon, not a gun. Get a vehicle, get up to speed near a pedestrian, and swing as you pass. It takes timing more than force: too slow and you miss, too fast and you cannot aim the swing. The bowling alley from Let's Go Bowling is a natural place to try it, but any road with foot traffic works.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: you can retry a melee drive-by as often as you like.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. PSN tracks this as a count to 250,000. Marked Bills come from robberies — bank vaults, armored trucks and the bigger heists — and they cannot be spent directly. Launder them through your contacts instead, turning dirty money into clean cash, and the count climbs with every batch. Rob often, launder everything, and this finishes long before the other money trophies. Which contacts launder bills has not been pinned down yet.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: it is cumulative and counts across the whole game.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. PSN tracks this as a count to 100,000. Buy weapons, clothes, cars and upgrades — every dollar spent in any shop counts toward the total. It builds up on its own if you play normally and keep your gear current; if you are short at the end, buy an expensive car or a round of top-tier weapon upgrades. There is no single shop to focus on — spread the spending wherever you like.

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. PSN tracks this as a count to 8 — eight garage properties. Garages are the properties that store your vehicle collection, and you buy them as you earn money. Eight in total, spread across Leonida, so keep an eye on the property listings as you travel. Save up before buying: garages are a big purchase, and this pairs naturally with Treat Yo Self, since every dollar spent counts there too.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: garage properties stay buyable after the story.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. PSN tracks this as a count to 10. Scooter Bros is the in-game phone app for vehicles — open it and register the vehicles you own or find. Ten registrations, so drive a variety of cars and bikes and register each new one as you go. It pairs with Whip It Good: every new vehicle you discover is also a candidate to register.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: the app stays available after the story.
